doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Conquering New York and the Metropole
summary: Coming with the Salt City Six, Longo became a Metropole house pianist playing with Red Allen, Hawkins and Krupa, working two shifts among drinkers.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Dizzy said it, “You’ve got to conquer New York.”
“You’ve got to conquer New York.” What’s the first step in conquering New York? If you come here maybe with a reputation with a few people, but boy it’s a big city, right?
Well what happened with me, the Salt City Six, I was trying to get here with them. So they were booked into the Metropole. I don’t know if you remember the Metropole.
I wanted to talk about that, yeah.

Okay. So what happened was the first night I played the Metropole Marty Napoleon was Louis Armstrong’s pianist at the time. And he was the house pianist there. And he went out in the neighborhood and next thing I knew man, about five piano players in the neighborhood were sitting there right at the bar listening to me play. And I said, “Man, this ain’t Florida, this is for me, New York.” And so when the Salt City Six left the Metropole hired me as one of the house pianists. I just stayed here. And that’s how it started. Except I was playing all the wrong kind of music. But I mean I was playing with some great people like Henry “Red” Allen, Coleman Hawkins, Gene Krupa, all those older cats.
I just wondered if you were like pinching yourself.
I was playing both shifts, man. I played from two in the afternoon ‘til eight at night with the older guys, and then at ten to four AM with Henry “Red” Allen at night. And so, there
